newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission bids to join Europe air safety body.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission bids to join Europe air safety body.

text.p: The European Commission launched a membership bid to join Europe's Joint Aviation Authorities (JAA) on Tuesday while urging that the body be given powers to draft and adopt binding air safety rules, a statement said.

Countries in the JAA, an informal grouping of national aviation authorities which was established in 1990, include the 15 European Union countries, Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Iceland, Malta, Monaco, Norway, Poland, Slovenia, Switzerland and Turkey.
Since 1991, the Commission has linked its own safety and technical harmonisation work to that of the JAA.
"This approach, however, is increasingly coming in for criticism from most interested parties," it added in reference to the airline industry, unions and management and air users.
Among the issues which have gone nowhere at the JAA is an attempt to reach agreement on pilot and flight-crew duty times.

The EU executive said the JAA should be able to adopt binding rules on aviation safety issues such as aircraft design, manufacture, operation and maintenance, and to cooperate with JAA members on uniform application of adopted rules.
The Commission's bid to join the JAA, reformed or otherwise, will hinge primarily on EU transport ministers' approval.
